content.text:
The user says: "The camera position in boss song when gameplay is too high that I can't see the hit position". So in boss gameplay, the camera is too high (looking down/up?) and they can't see the hit position (the lane rings at the bottom are cut off / too low? "camera position ... too high" meaning camera is positioned too high, so the hit line/rings are too low or off-screen).

Looking at the APOTHEOSIS screenshot: the rings at the bottom are near the bottom edge, and in the 4-lane play screenshot, rings are at y~550 of 640 (~86% height), close to the bottom. The pads are anchored there. On mobile, rings are at y~650 of 844 (77%). The user says "camera position too high that I can't see the hit position" — likely on their device (maybe landscape phone or a shorter screen), the hit line is below the viewport / obscured. Or perhaps the camera looks too high so the hit line is at the very bottom, hidden under the HUD or safe area.

We need to adjust boss gameplay cameras to frame the hit line higher on screen. The issue is that boss camera events use fixed look targets (e.g., look [0,5.4,-3]) and positions at y7-11; the hit rings are at y=0, z near 0, projected low. Other tracks use camera y6.7 camZ17.2 look at y4.05, projecting rings ~65% down.

In boss play, camera positions around y7.4-9.8, look y5.4-7, sometimes look y5.2 and z-3..-10, and fov 46-53. The rings at y0, z~0: with camera at y8.1, z18.4 looking at (0,5.4,-3), the ring at y0 z0 is below the look direction, maybe ~80-90% down. In the screenshot, yes rings at ~86%.

So we need to raise the ring position on screen by lowering the look target or raising camera pitch less? Wait, to see the hit position higher (further from bottom), the camera should look lower (more downward) so the hit line moves toward center. If the camera looks at a lower y (e.g., look y2 instead of 5.4), the rings at y0 will be closer to screen center, and the clock moves up/off-screen. But we want the clock still visible.

Alternatively, camera could be lower (y smaller?) and look at y2, keeping the clock up. Let's reason with the projection: camera at (0,8.1,18.4), looking at (0,5.4,-3), direction mostly -z with slight downward. Ring at (0,0,0.24) is below the view center. If we change look to (0,2.5,-3), the view center points more downward; the ring at y0 will be above center (maybe 45% height), and the clock at y10,z-39 will be higher on screen (possibly cropped). We can compensate by moving the camera back / down or adjusting FOV to include the clock.

Since the boss stage is a tall scene, we need to frame both clock (y10, z-39) and rings (y0, z0) in the view. Vertical angular span from camera (0,8.1,18.4): clock center angle atan((10-8.1)/57.4)=1.9° above horizontal; ring angle atan((0-8.1)/18.4)= -23.7° below horizontal. So the span is ~25.6°. With fov 46°, it should fit. The look direction is currently at atan((5.4-8.1)/21.4) = -7.2°. The view vertical range is -7.2±23 = +15.8° to -30.2°. Ring at -23.7° → relative position (−23.7+7.2)/46 = -0.359 below center? Projection y_screen = 0.5 + tan(angle relative)*... For small angles, relative = (-23.7 - (-7.2))/46 = -0.359 → y = 0.5+0.359 = 0.859 (86%). Exactly. To place the ring at 75%, we need the look angle lower by ~5°: look y ~3.4 at z-3 (angle -11.7°), then ring at (23.7-11.7)/46=0.261 → 76%. The clock angle 1.9° becomes (1.9+11.7)/46=0.296 above center → 20% from top, still visible. That's good. The clock currently at (1.9+7.2)/46=0.198 above center → 30% from top (in screenshots, clock center ~35% from top). Lowering the look moves the clock up to ~20%, which may crop the top of the large rose halo but the clock itself still fits (radius 10.5 at distance 57 = 10.4°; top relative (1.9+10.4+11.7)/46 = 0.52 → just above top? Actually 0.5-0.52 = -0.02, slightly cropped at top. The clock's top rim would be at the very top. Hmm, the clock scale is large. We might also move the camera back slightly (z +2) to reduce both.

But the user says "camera position ... too high" — maybe they mean the camera itself is too high, so the hit line is far below and partially hidden behind the bottom HUD/pads? The fix could be to lower the camera and look down more, which brings the hit line up.

Let me replicate the issue precisely with the actual layout in a typical viewport. The user may play on desktop 16:9 or mobile. In our desktop 1440×900 screenshots, the rings are visible at y~760/900 = 84%, just above the bottom 40px hint maybe. On a 1280×720 or a phone landscape, vertical FOV constant 46° but aspect changes; rings remain at 84% (same vertical), visible. On mobile portrait, rings at 77%. So why "can't see the hit position"? Maybe the rings are partially behind the mobile bottom safe area / the "8 LANES" hint / browser chrome. On mobile, the viewport height in the app is 844; rings at ~650 (77%), not cut.

Wait—maybe the camera events after APOTHEOSIS are different: by mid-HUNT, camera pos y10.2 look y4.6, fov53 → rings even lower? Let's compute HUNT event at 83.03: pos (0,10.2,13.8), look (0,4.6,-8), fov53. Ring angle atan(-10.2/13.8)=-36.5°; look angle atan((4.6-10.2)/21.8)=-14.4°; relative (36.5-14.4)/53=0.417 → 92% down! That's likely the problem: in HUNT/FINALE, the camera is closer (z 13-15) and higher (y10-11), with a fov 51-53, pushing rings to 90-95% down, below the visible area or behind the control hint. Indeed, the APOTHEOSIS screenshot showed rings at ~93%? In the 1440x900 shot scaled to 1024x640, rings appear around y550-600 = 86-94%. The bottom labels are cut. So yes, later sections have the hit line too low. The user likely experienced this.

We need to fix boss camera framing, especially for later sections. Best approach: rather than editing every chart event, adjust the boss camera rendering so the hit line is guaranteed to be at a comfortable screen height (e.g., 72-78%). Options:

A) Modify chart camera events' look y / add pitch offset in scene for boss gameplay. In `bossCameraEvent`, we can apply a vertical framing correction: subtract a pitch offset from the look target, or in the camera update, add a bias. But the events were designed to frame the clock; a global downward shift may crop the clock.

B) Dynamically compute the look target to keep both clock and hit line in frame: clamp the camera pitch so the ring projections stay above 80% and the clock top stays below ~5%. This can be done in the camera update for boss play (mode 'play'/'outro'): after lerping to the event target, adjust `camera.lookAt` to a compensated look point. But events are authored. Simpler: lower the camera y by a factor and raise the look target? Let's analyze.

To bring the hit line up while keeping the clock visible, decrease camera height (closer to the ring plane) and look slightly down. If the camera y is lower, the ring angle below horizon decreases (less negative), so the ring moves up; the clock angle above horizon increases, moving the clock up too. That worsens the clock cropping. Alternatively, increasing camera distance (z) reduces both angles: ring moves up, clock moves down (toward center). That's ideal: move the camera back (increase z) for later events. But the camera events have z 11-15 (close, cinematic), which is why the rings are low. Moving back to z 17-19 would fix it, at the cost of a less dramatic push-in.

For example, HUNT event pos (0,10.2,13.8) → if we scale z to 18.5 and y to 8.2:
- ring angle atan(-8.2/18.5)=-23.9°
- look target maybe (0,4.6,-8) angle atan((4.6-8.2)/26.5)=-7.7°
- relative (23.9-7.7)/53 = 0.306 → 81% (a bit high but visible)
- clock at y10.4,z-39: angle atan(2.2/57.5)=2.2°; relative above center (2.2+7.7)/53=0.187 → 31% from top; clock radius angle 10.4° adds 0.196 → top at 11% from top. Good, clock fits.

So a global "pull back and lower" for boss camera events would fix framing. But modifying the authored chart coordinates is easiest in the chart builder, but we'd need to regenerate the chart. Alternatively, apply a transform in `bossCameraEvent` or the camera update:
- Scale z position outward relative to the stage: `z' = z + 4` and reduce y by ~2? But the events include shots from z -14, +16 (around the church) during intro; for gameplay events z 11-20. We only need to adjust during gameplay (mode play/outro) and maybe intro's prebeat. Applying only when boss.mode === 'play' works.
- In `bossCameraEvent`, if boss.mode === 'play' (but at the time event 28.49 fires, mode may still be intro until bossPhase; bossPhase is after bossCamera in the chart, so mode is 'intro' for the first play event; subsequent events mode='play'). Could apply whenever the event is a gameplay-stage event based on the look/coords? Simpler: adjust all `bossCameraEvent` calls while `boss.active` and not `boss.intro`? At the first event mode might be intro. Hmm.

Better: implement a framing solver in the animation loop for boss play/outro: after computing the camera position/look/FOV from events, enforce a screen-space rule:
- Project the hit line point (0,0,0.24) and the clock top (0, 10.4 + 10.5, -39) with the current camera; if the hit line's screen y > 0.82 (too low), adjust the camera's look point upward? Wait adjusting look up moves everything down (worse). To move the hit line up, look *down* (target y lower). The clock top then moves up. If clock top goes off-screen, pull the camera back, which simultaneously moves the hit line up and clock down. So:
  1. Determine y_screen of ring. If > 0.80, we need more downward look and/or farther z.
  2. Pull camera back along z (away from rig) until the ring angle is reduced. This requires modifying position z, which breaks the authored move (but only modestly).
  
Simplest and most controllable: adjust the authored gameplay camera events in the chart generator to use higher/farther cameras for late sections. But there are 24 play events; editing the generator then regenerating the chart is doable. But scene-side transform is easier and applies to all.

Alternative: change the **camera projection** to shift the image vertically, e.g., `camera.setViewOffset` or film offset. This is elegant: apply an optical shift so the hit line appears higher without moving the camera or clock relative to each other. If we shift the rendered image downward (i.e., move the principal point up?), the whole scene moves up on screen: both clock and rings move up. The clock top may crop, but the clock is usually at 30% and can move up ~8%; the ring moves from 90% to 82%. We need more than 8% for some events. Also cropping the clock top is acceptable? The user wants hit position; the clock can be partly cropped at the top. But the top HUD/progress overlays there.

Better: combine a modest camera pullback + optical shift. But maybe a simpler fix: **lower the lane rings' world z?** No, gameplay physics/timing rely on y.

We could move the stage itself up in screen space by adjusting camera look at a lower y for the entire boss stage. Let's test with the worst event (HUNT 83.03): pos (0,10.2,13.8) look (0,4.6,-8), fov53. If we lower the look target by 6 units to (0,-1.4,-8): look angle atan(-11.6/21.8)=-28°; ring angle -36.5°; relative (36.5-28)/53=0.16 → 66% (great); clock center angle 1.9°; relative (1.9+28)/53=0.56 → above top (clock center off-screen). Bad. So lowering look alone loses the clock. If we also pull back to z=22 while keeping y=10.2? Ring angle atan(-10.2/22)=-24.9; look angle atan((4.6-10.2)/30)=-10.6; relative 27%; clock angle atan(0.2/61)=0.2; relative (0.2+10.6)/53=20% from center top... clock top +9.8 → 39%? So pulling camera z back to ~22 (from 13.8) fixes it while keeping the clock. That changes the composition to a wider shot but still cinematic.

The HUNT camera is intentionally close for intensity; but playability matters. We can apply a **minimum camera distance from the stage** for boss gameplay: distance along z at least ~18-20. The authored z ranges 11.2-19.2 for play events (some already 19-20). Set z = max(z, 18.5) for play mode; maybe also lower camera y slightly? With z=18.5 for HUNT (y10.2): ring angle atan(-10.2/18.5)=-28.9; look atan((4.6-10.2)/26.5)=-12.1; relative (28.9-12.1)/53=0.317 → 82%; clock top: center atan(0.2/57.5)=0.2; top angle 10.4; relative (0.2+10.4+12.1)/53=0.429 → 7% from top. const bossFrameV = new THREE.Vector3();

// Solving helpers -------------------------------------------------
// Vertical field of view (deg) needed to hold the hit rings at `ringFrac`
// and the clock crown at `crownFrac` from a camera at (x, y, z).
function bossVerticalFov(x, y, z, crown, ringFrac, crownFrac) {
  const ringD = Math.hypot(x - BOSS_RING.x, z - BOSS_RING.z);
  const crownD = Math.hypot(x - crown.x, z - crown.z);
  const a = Math.atan2(BOSS_RING.y - y, ringD);
  const b = Math.atan2(crown.y - y, crownD);
  const span = b - a;
  const ndcRing = 1 - 2 * ringFrac;
  const ndcCrown = 1 - 2 * crownFrac;
  let lo = 0.01, hi = 6;
  for (let i = 0; i < 26; i++) {
    const T = (lo + hi) * 0.5;
    if (Math.atan(-ndcRing * T) + Math.atan(ndcCrown * T) < span) lo = T;
    else hi = T;
  }
  return 2 * Math.atan((lo + hi) * 0.5) * RAD2DEG;
}
```

Then s(1 - m T²) = k T → s m T² + k T - s = 0 → T = (-k + sqrt(k² + 4 s² m)) / (2 s m). But span can exceed 90° and tan blows up; bisection is safer. 26 iterations * small = fine.

content.text:
### Gameplay

- **Track selection:** pick any of the four tracks from the start screen. Audio decodes per track and is cached, and personal bests are stored per track in `localStorage`.
- **Dynamic lane count:** charts move through 4, 6, and 8-lane sections; the field spacing, ring scale, note scale, camera and hit zones re-frame themselves around the playable lanes.
- **Tap the whole lane:** invisible tap strips start at the hit circle, run straight up the lane along its projected angle, extend below the ring for thumbs, and widen to fill the gap between neighbouring lanes. Pressing never draws an overlay — all feedback is in the 3D field.
- **Incoming lanes unlock early:** a lane with a note on the way becomes tappable before its section officially starts, so notes never arrive on a hidden lane.
- **Holds:** keep at least one finger anywhere on the screen to sustain every active hold. Releasing one thumb won't break another lane's hold.
- **Moving lanes:** lanes fan, wave, slope, zigzag, and orbit with each section; notes and hold bodies are parented to the lane frame so they follow the same diagonal.
- **Unused-lane echoes:** dormant lanes emit directional beat echoes that drift sideways, slow down, and fade.
- **City intro:** the second track layers a two-plane parallax skyline behind the field during its intro, break, and outro.
- **Clockwork background:** CHRONOSTASIS turns the two unused outer lanes into a background clock. The slow hand sweeps while the fast hand ticks on the beat; the chart starts the clock at motif boundaries, freezes it during the breakdown, and speeds it up for the final section.
- **Frozen pendulum:** during the STASIS breakdown the clock stops and one lane becomes an antique pendulum. It swings left and right over a centre target while music-note glyphs float around it; tap the centre (click/tap the target or press `Space`) each time the bob crosses the middle. The gimmick runs until the next clock event and then hands the screen back to the lane chart.
- **Cathedral overture:** THE UNTOUCHABLE opens with 28.5 lane-less seconds inside a procedural gothic nave. The camera cuts down the aisle on the beat, stained glass and title cards carry the story, and the playfield stays hidden until the clock chamber arrives.
- **Wind instead of idle lanes:** in the boss stage any lane that is not playable becomes a stream of 3D wind ribbons that sweep through X, Y and Z while spinning, so the unused field is part of the scene instead of empty tracks.
- **Free-flight clock stage:** after the overture the nave becomes the playfield and notes travel on curved X/Z paths before converging on their lane rings at the hit line. The boss chart follows a 111.1 → 96 → 111.1 BPM map, and every camera, glitch, caption and clock tick event is keyed to the analysed song.
- **Feedback:** perfect/great/good/bad/miss windows, combo, score, accuracy, sync meter, hit bursts, shockwaves, screen flashes, and rank screen.
- **Results:** animated “COMPILING RESULTS” transition followed by a full results layout with score, accuracy ring, judgement bars, combo trace, rank, and new-best delta.
- **Pause safely:** `Esc` or the pause button freezes both the transport and the chart; switching tabs/windows pauses automatically.
- **Responsive:** landscape and portrait layouts, safe-area padding, multi-touch pointer capture, no page scrolling during play.

20: ## CRYOUT — Dynamic 3D Rhythm
21: 
22: A browser rhythm game built around a flat, bold hit-circle language placed inside a moving 3D field. Four fully charted tracks are included, each with its own section map, lane motion, effects, and difficulty curve.
23: 
24: ### Tracks
25: 
26: | Track | BPM | Difficulty | Lanes | Notes |
27: | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
28: | **CRYOUT** | 100 | Advanced | 4 · 6 · 8 | 328 notes · 6 holds |
29: | **WORLD YEARNING FOR AN END** | 120 | Hard | 4 · 6 | 448 notes · 5 holds |
30: | **CHRONOSTASIS** | 99.4 | Expert | 4 · 6 | 432 notes · 1 hold · 8 pendulum taps |
31: | **THE UNTOUCHABLE OF f RA IA'S LAND** | 111.1 / 96 | Boss | 4 · 6 · 8 | 407 notes · 4 holds · 243 events |
32: 
33: Charts are generated offline from beat/onset analysis, then committed as static data in `src/charts/`. Each track has its own event recipe: CRYOUT keeps its authored 4/6/8-lane chart and signal accents, WORLD uses city/atmospheric accents, CHRONOSTASIS derives its ticks, bursts, clock windows, and pendulum taps from its analysed motif peaks, and THE UNTOUCHABLE is built from a dedicated onset analysis with an explicit tempo map. Track metadata lives in `src/tracks.js`.
34: 
35: ### Gameplay
36: 
37: - **Track selection:** pick any of the four tracks from the start screen. Audio decodes per track and is cached, and personal bests are stored per track in `localStorage`.
38: - **Dynamic lane count:** charts move through 4, 6, and 8-lane sections; the field spacing, ring scale, note scale, camera and hit zones re-frame themselves around the playable lanes.
39: - **Tap the whole lane:** invisible tap strips start at the hit circle, run straight up the lane along its projected angle, extend below the ring for thumbs, and widen to fill the gap between neighbouring lanes. Pressing never draws an overlay — all feedback is in the 3D field.
40: - **Incoming lanes unlock early:** a lane with a note on the way becomes tappable before its section officially starts, so notes never arrive on a hidden lane.
41: - **Holds:** keep at least one finger anywhere on the screen to sustain every active hold. Releasing one thumb won't break another lane's hold.
42: - **Moving lanes:** lanes fan, wave, slope, zigzag, and orbit with each section; notes and hold bodies are parented to the lane frame so they follow the same diagonal.
43: - **Unused-lane echoes:** dormant lanes emit directional beat echoes that drift sideways, slow down, and fade.
44: - **City intro:** the second track layers a two-plane parallax skyline behind the field during its intro, break, and outro.
45: - **Clockwork background:** CHRONOSTASIS turns the two unused outer lanes into a background clock. The slow hand sweeps while the fast hand ticks on the beat; the chart starts the clock at motif boundaries, freezes it during the breakdown, and speeds it up for the final section.
46: - **Frozen pendulum:** during the STASIS breakdown the clock stops and one lane becomes an antique pendulum. It swings left and right over a centre target while music-note glyphs float around it; tap the centre (click/tap the target or press `Space`) each time the bob crosses the middle. The gimmick runs until the next clock event and then hands the screen back to the lane chart.
47: - **Cathedral overture:** THE UNTOUCHABLE opens with 28.5 lane-less seconds inside a procedural gothic nave. The camera cuts down the aisle on the beat, stained glass and title cards carry the story, and the playfield stays hidden until the clock chamber arrives.
48: - **Wind instead of idle lanes:** in the boss stage any lane that is not playable becomes a stream of 3D wind ribbons that sweep through X, Y and Z while spinning, so the unused field is part of the scene instead of empty tracks.
49: - **Free-flight clock stage:** after the overture the nave becomes the playfield and notes travel on curved X/Z paths before converging on their lane rings at the hit line. The boss chart follows a 111.1 → 96 → 111.1 BPM map, and every camera, glitch, caption and clock tick event is keyed to the analysed song. A framing guard measures the live rings and the clock crown after each authored camera move, then only adjusts pitch, lens or distance when the hit line or the crown would leave the frame, so the cinematic direction survives on desktop and phone aspect ratios.
50: - **Feedback:** perfect/great/good/bad/miss windows, combo, score, accuracy, sync meter, hit bursts, shockwaves, screen flashes, and rank screen.
51: - **Results:** animated “COMPILING RESULTS” transition followed by a full results layout with score, accuracy ring, judgement bars, combo trace, rank, and new-best delta.
52: - **Pause safely:** `Esc` or the pause button freezes both the transport and the chart; switching tabs/windows pauses automatically.
53: - **Responsive:** landscape and portrait layouts, safe-area padding, multi-touch pointer capture, no page scrolling during play.
54: 
55: ### Controls
56: 
57: `A S D F J K L ;`, numpad `1–8`, or tap/click anywhere along a lane. During CHRONOSTASIS's STASIS breakdown, `Space` or a tap on the centre target hits the pendulum. `Esc` pauses.
58: 
59: ### Development
60: 
61: ```bash
62: npm install
63: npm run dev     # http://localhost:3002
64: npm run build   # static bundle in dist/
65: ```
66: 
67: The playfield is Three.js with an Unreal Bloom pass; audio transport is Web Audio so pause/resume freezes the chart and the music together.
68:

70: 
71: ```bash
72: node tools/analyze-audio.mjs input.wav analysis.json
73: node tools/build-charts.mjs cryout-analysis.json world-analysis.json chronostasis-analysis.json
74: node tools/build-boss-chart.mjs   # reads tools/source/untouchable-onsets.json

await page.evaluate(() => {
  const c = window.__cryout;
  const codes = ['KeyA','KeyS','KeyD','KeyF','KeyJ','KeyK','KeyL','Semicolon'];
  const now = c.audio.time;
  const key = (type, code) => document.dispatchEvent(new KeyboardEvent(type, {code, bubbles:true, cancelable:true}));
  // group per lane
  const lanes = Array.from({length:8},()=>[]);
  for (const n of c.chart.notes) lanes[n.lane].push(n);
  for (let l=0;l<8;l++) lanes[l].sort((a,b)=>a.t-b.t);
  const timers=[];
  const at = (t, fn) => { const d=(t-now)*1000; timers.push(setTimeout(fn, Math.max(0,d))); };
  for (let l=0;l<8;l++) {
    const list=lanes[l];
    for (let i=0;i<list.length;i++){
      const n=list[i];
      const next=list[i+1];
      at(n.t-0.012, ()=>key('keydown', codes[l]));
      const holdEnd = n.type==='hold' ? n.t+(n.dur||0)+0.06 : n.t+0.06;
      const nextPress = next ? next.t-0.02 : Infinity;
      const up = Math.min(holdEnd, nextPress);
      at(up, ()=>key('keyup', codes[l]));
    }
  }
  for (const s of (c.chart.swings||[])) at(s.t-0.012, ()=>key('keydown', 'Space'));
  for (const s of (c.chart.swings||[])) at(s.t+0.06, ()=>key('keyup', 'Space'));
  return {notes:c.chart.notes.length, swings:(c.chart.swings||[]).length};
});

Each track has its own event recipe: CRYOUT keeps its authored 4/6/8-lane chart and signal accents, WORLD uses city/atmospheric accents, CHRONOSTASIS derives its ticks, bursts, clock windows, and pendulum taps from its analysed motif peaks, and THE UNTOUCHABLE is built from a dedicated onset analysis with an explicit tempo map. +- **Track selection:** pick any of the four tracks from the start screen. Audio decodes per track and is cached, and personal bests are stored per track in `localStorage`. A run that clears a track (50% accuracy or better) marks its card, and the picker header tracks how many of the four have been cleared.
 - **Dynamic lane count:** charts move through 4, 6, and 8-lane sections; the field spacing, ring scale, note scale, camera and hit zones re-frame themselves around the playable lanes.
 - **Tap the whole lane:** invisible tap strips start at the hit circle, run straight up the lane along its projected angle, extend below the ring for thumbs, and widen to fill the gap between neighbouring lanes. Pressing never draws an overlay — all feedback is in the 3D field.
 - **Incoming lanes unlock early:** a lane with a note on the way becomes tappable before its section officially starts, so notes never arrive on a hidden lane.
 - **Holds:** keep at least one finger anywhere on the screen to sustain every active hold. Releasing one thumb won't break another lane's hold.

## Objective
- Add “Intention” as a new 180 BPM boss track in CRYOUT, with its own chart, visuals, camera choreography, gameplay gimmicks, and GUILT-style meter.
- Preserve the existing tracks and gameplay.

## Requirements
- Open with white and black lanes against a black, floating-particle scene; around 0:17.5 reveal an ocean-above view with blue sky, dark clouds, floating flowers, and a golden Libra.
- At 0:29, rapidly spin and zoom toward one lane, reset to four lanes, and bounce the lanes on the beat.
- At 0:46, begin a boss sequence with four differently sized cardinal-direction pillars, flashes, and a camera that follows hit positions; transition to a top-down Libra view with a spinning halo-star and glitching “INTENTIONS” text.
- Before 1:12, distort and darken the screen, then show a beat-synced heartbeat animation.
- At 1:14.5, show a black screen with a red GUILT bar that drains and refills on consistent perfect play, draining more slowly when fewer notes are incoming; keep the heartbeat.
- On “Ready,” gradually raise BPM toward 195, increase note speed and density, focus play on one lane, and add screen glitch. Around 1:28, add a two-lane glitch-note pattern requiring hits on the fourth beat but using a different rhythm. After another “Ready,” return to the fast one-lane pattern until about 1:40.
- At 1:40, distort the camera; at 1:44, return to the ocean. At 1:57, float a GUILT memory upward with subtle transparent static.
- At 2:37, restore normal effects with bright, determined visuals. At 3:01, turn the screen white and hide lanes; at 3:02, show black four-lane gameplay with glitching and a decorative, slowly draining low GUILT bar that nearly shatters but does not refill.
- At 3:24.5, regain consciousness; at 3:25, use a yellow vignette, return to the ocean, hide notes, add more flowers, and make the sync bar rainbow/full.
- “the hold note less generate at a part that suitable for many hold notes,fix that ....” Reduce holds outside suitable sections and add them where the music supports them.
- Use the supplied video as reference for the two-lane gimmick.

## Decisions
- Treat the supplied audio as 213.505 seconds long; timestamps are minutes:seconds, including apparent typos such as “0:175” and “1:145.”
- Use offline audio analysis to guide tempo and charting, while still checking the audio and reference video.

- Existing four-track game, including “The Untouchable of f RA IA’s Land,” is integrated; prior checks reported perfect autoplay clears for all four tracks.

A browser rhythm game built around a flat, bold hit-circle language placed inside a moving 3D field. Four fully charted tracks are included, each with its own section map, lane motion, effects, and difficulty curve.

### Tracks

| Track | BPM | Difficulty | Lanes | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **CRYOUT** | 100 | Advanced | 4 · 6 · 8 | 328 notes · 6 holds |
| **WORLD YEARNING FOR AN END** | 120 | Hard | 4 · 6 | 448 notes · 5 holds |
| **CHRONOSTASIS** | 99.4 | Expert | 4 · 6 | 432 notes · 1 hold · 8 pendulum taps |
| **THE UNTOUCHABLE OF f RA IA'S LAND** | 111.1 / 96 | Boss | 4 · 6 · 8 | 407 notes · 4 holds · 243 events |

Charts are generated offline from beat/onset analysis, then committed as static data in `src/charts/`. Each track has its own event recipe: CRYOUT keeps its authored 4/6/8-lane chart and signal accents, WORLD uses city/atmospheric accents, CHRONOSTASIS derives its ticks, bursts, clock windows, and pendulum taps from its analysed motif peaks, and THE UNTOUCHABLE is built from a dedicated onset analysis with an explicit tempo map. Track metadata lives in `src/tracks.js`.

### Gameplay

- **Track selection:** pick any of the four tracks from the start screen. Audio decodes per track and is cached, and personal bests are stored per track in `localStorage`. A run that clears a track (50% accuracy or better) marks its card, and the picker header tracks how many of the four have been cleared.
- **Dynamic lane count:** charts move through 4, 6, and 8-lane sections; the field spacing, ring scale, note scale, camera and hit zones re-frame themselves around the playable lanes.
- **Tap the whole lane:** invisible tap strips start at the hit circle, run straight up the lane along its projected angle, extend below the ring for thumbs, and widen to fill the gap between neighbouring lanes. Pressing never draws an overlay — all feedback is in the 3D field.
- **Incoming lanes unlock early:** a lane with a note on the way becomes tappable before its section officially starts, so notes never arrive on a hidden lane.
- **Holds:** keep at least one finger anywhere on the screen to sustain every active hold. Releasing one thumb won't break another lane's hold.
- **Moving lanes:** lanes fan, wave, slope, zigzag, and orbit with each section; notes and hold bodies are parented to the lane frame so they follow the same diagonal.
- **Unused-lane echoes:** dormant lanes emit directional beat echoes that drift sideways, slow down, and fade.
- **City intro:** the second track layers a two-plane parallax skyline behind the field during its intro, break, and outro.
- **Clockwork background:** CHRONOSTASIS turns the two unused outer lanes into a background clock. The slow hand sweeps while the fast hand ticks on the beat; the chart starts the clock at motif boundaries, freezes it during the breakdown, and speeds it up for the final section.
- **Frozen pendulum:** during the STASIS breakdown the clock stops and one lane becomes an antique pendulum. It swings left and right over a centre target while music-note glyphs float around it; tap the centre (click/tap the target or press `Space`) each time the bob crosses the middle. The gimmick runs until the next clock event and then hands the screen back to the lane chart.
- **Cathedral overture:** THE UNTOUCHABLE opens with 28.5 lane-less seconds inside a procedural gothic nave. The camera cuts down the aisle on the beat, stained glass and title cards carry the story, and the playfield stays hidden until the clock chamber arrives.
- **Wind instead of idle lanes:** in the boss stage any lane that is not playable becomes a stream of 3D wind ribbons that sweep through X, Y and Z while spinning, so the unused field is part of the scene instead of empty tracks.
- **Free-flight clock stage:** after the overture the nave becomes the playfield and notes travel on curved X/Z paths before converging on their lane rings at the hit line. The boss chart follows a 111.1 → 96 → 111.1 BPM map, and every camera, glitch, caption and clock tick event is keyed to the analysed song. A framing guard measures the live rings and the clock crown after each authored camera move, then only adjusts pitch, lens or distance when the hit line or the crown would leave the frame, so the cinematic direction survives on desktop and phone aspect ratios.
- **Feedback:** perfect/great/good/bad/miss windows, combo, score, accuracy, sync meter, hit bursts, shockwaves, screen flashes, and rank screen.
- **Results:** animated “COMPILING RESULTS” transition followed by a full results layout with score, accuracy ring, judgement bars, combo trace, rank, and new-best delta.
- **Pause safely:** `Esc` or the pause button freezes both the transport and the chart; switching tabs/windows pauses automatically.
- **Responsive:** landscape and portrait layouts, safe-area padding, multi-touch pointer capture, no page scrolling during play.

### Controls

`A S D F J K L ;`, numpad `1–8`, or tap/click anywhere along a lane. During CHRONOSTASIS's STASIS breakdown, `Space` or a tap on the centre target hits the pendulum. `Esc` pauses.

### Development

```bash
npm install
npm run dev     # http://localhost:3002
npm run build   # static bundle in dist/
```

The playfield is Three.js with an Unreal Bloom pass; audio transport is Web Audio so pause/resume freezes the chart and the music together.

### Chart tooling

```bash
node tools/analyze-audio.mjs input.wav analysis.json
node tools/build-charts.mjs cryout-analysis.json world-analysis.json chronostasis-analysis.json
node tools/build-boss-chart.mjs   # reads tools/source/untouchable-onsets.json
```

The original Cryout chart is preserved in `tools/source/cryout-legacy.json`. The analyser reads mono 16-bit WAV; the repository MP3s can be decoded to that format offline before analysis. The chart builder derives clock windows and accents from detected motif peaks, so adding another song does not reuse the same event layout. The boss chart builder maps the overture, clock chamber and finale onto the analysed onset grid and writes the full event score used by the cathedral stage.

## Objective
- Finish the CRYOUT game by adding “Intention” as a complete 180 BPM boss track with its own chart, visuals, camera choreography, gameplay gimmicks, and GUILT-style meter.
- Preserve the existing tracks and gameplay.

## Requirements
- Open with white and black lanes against a black, floating-particle scene; around 0:17.5 reveal an ocean-above view with blue sky, dark clouds, floating flowers, and a golden Libra.
- At 0:29, rapidly spin and zoom toward one lane, reset to four lanes, and bounce the lanes on the beat.
- At 0:46, begin a boss sequence with four differently sized cardinal-direction pillars, flashes, and a camera that follows hit positions; transition to a top-down Libra view with a spinning halo-star and glitching “INTENTIONS” text.
- Before 1:12, distort and darken the screen, then show a beat-synced heartbeat animation.
- At 1:14.5, show a black screen with a red GUILT bar that drains and refills on consistent perfect play, draining more slowly when fewer notes are incoming; keep the heartbeat.
- On “Ready,” gradually raise BPM toward 195, increase note speed and density, focus play on one lane, and add screen glitch. Around 1:28, add a two-lane glitch-note pattern requiring hits on the fourth beat but using a different rhythm. After another “Ready,” return to the fast one-lane pattern until about 1:40.
- At 1:40, distort the camera; at 1:44, return to the ocean. At 1:57, float a GUILT memory upward with subtle transparent static.
- At 2:37, restore normal effects with bright, determined visuals. At 3:01, turn the screen white and hide lanes; at 3:02, show black four-lane gameplay with glitching and a decorative, slowly draining low GUILT bar that nearly shatters but does not refill.
- At 3:24.5, regain consciousness; at 3:25, use a yellow vignette, return to the ocean, hide notes, add more flowers, and make the sync bar rainbow/full.
- Reduce holds outside suitable sections and add them where the music supports them.
- Use the supplied video as reference for the two-lane gimmick.

## Decisions
- Treat the supplied audio as 213.505 seconds long; timestamps are minutes:seconds, including apparent typos such as “0:175” and “1:145.”
- Use offline audio analysis to guide tempo and charting, while still checking the audio and reference video.

## Work State
### Completed
- Existing four-track game, including “The Untouchable of f RA IA’s Land,” is integrated; prior checks reported perfect autoplay clears for all four tracks.

<!-- omgithub:readme:end -->

## CRYOUT — Dynamic 3D Rhythm

A browser rhythm game built around a flat, bold hit-circle language placed inside a moving 3D field. Five fully charted tracks are included, each with its own section map, lane motion, effects, and difficulty curve.

### Tracks

| Track | BPM | Difficulty | Lanes | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **CRYOUT** | 100 | Advanced | 4 · 6 · 8 | 328 notes · 6 holds |
| **WORLD YEARNING FOR AN END** | 120 | Hard | 4 · 6 | 448 notes · 5 holds |
| **CHRONOSTASIS** | 99.4 | Expert | 4 · 6 | 432 notes · 1 hold · 8 pendulum taps |
| **THE UNTOUCHABLE OF f RA IA'S LAND** | 111.1 / 96 | Boss | 4 · 6 · 8 | 407 notes · 4 holds · 243 events |
| **INTENTION** | 180 / 195 | Boss | 1 · 2 · 4 · 6 | 596 notes · 26 holds · 239 events |

Charts are generated offline from beat/onset analysis, then committed as static data in `src/charts/`. Each track has its own event recipe: CRYOUT keeps its authored 4/6/8-lane chart and signal accents, WORLD uses city/atmospheric accents, CHRONOSTASIS derives its ticks, bursts, clock windows, and pendulum taps from its analysed motif peaks, and THE UNTOUCHABLE is built from a dedicated onset analysis with an explicit tempo map. INTENTION uses a dedicated onset/tempo analysis and an event score for its ocean, libra, guilt and dawn movements. Track metadata lives in `src/tracks.js`.

### Gameplay

- **Track selection:** pick any of the five tracks from the start screen. Audio decodes per track and is cached, and personal bests are stored per track in `localStorage`. A run that clears a track (50% accuracy or better) marks its card, and the picker header tracks how many of the five have been cleared.
- **Dynamic lane count:** charts move through 4, 6, and 8-lane sections; the field spacing, ring scale, note scale, camera and hit zones re-frame themselves around the playable lanes.
- **Tap the whole lane:** invisible tap strips start at the hit circle, run straight up the lane along its projected angle, extend below the ring for thumbs, and widen to fill the gap between neighbouring lanes. Pressing never draws an overlay — all feedback is in the 3D field.
- **Incoming lanes unlock early:** a lane with a note on the way becomes tappable before its section officially starts, so notes never arrive on a hidden lane.
- **Holds:** keep at least one finger anywhere on the screen to sustain every active hold. Releasing one thumb won't break another lane's hold.
- **Moving lanes:** lanes fan, wave, slope, zigzag, and orbit with each section; notes and hold bodies are parented to the lane frame so they follow the same diagonal.
- **Unused-lane echoes:** dormant lanes emit directional beat echoes that drift sideways, slow down, and fade.
- **City intro:** the second track layers a two-plane parallax skyline behind the field during its intro, break, and outro.
- **Clockwork background:** CHRONOSTASIS turns the two unused outer lanes into a background clock. The slow hand sweeps while the fast hand ticks on the beat; the chart starts the clock at motif boundaries, freezes it during the breakdown, and speeds it up for the final section.
- **Frozen pendulum:** during the STASIS breakdown the clock stops and one lane becomes an antique pendulum. It swings left and right over a centre target while music-note glyphs float around it; tap the centre (click/tap the target or press `Space`) each time the bob crosses the middle. The gimmick runs until the next clock event and then hands the screen back to the lane chart.
- **Cathedral overture:** THE UNTOUCHABLE opens with 28.5 lane-less seconds inside a procedural gothic nave. The camera cuts down the aisle on the beat, stained glass and title cards carry the story, and the playfield stays hidden until the clock chamber arrives.
- **Wind instead of idle lanes:** in the boss stage any lane that is not playable becomes a stream of 3D wind ribbons that sweep through X, Y and Z while spinning, so the unused field is part of the scene instead of empty tracks.
- **Free-flight clock stage:** after the overture the nave becomes the playfield and notes travel on curved X/Z paths before converging on their lane rings at the hit line. The boss chart follows a 111.1 → 96 → 111.1 BPM map, and every camera, glitch, caption and clock tick event is keyed to the analysed song. A framing guard measures the live rings and the clock crown after each authored camera move, then only adjusts pitch, lens or distance when the hit line or the crown would leave the frame, so the cinematic direction survives on desktop and phone aspect ratios.
- **INTENTION's four memories:** a black-particle overture with white lanes opens onto an ocean under dark clouds, a golden libra, four cardinal pillars, and a spinning halo star. A one-lane corkscrew snaps back to the field, the camera leans toward the lane that just answered, and the top-down libra shot carries a glitching INTENTIONS title. The chart then distorts into a heartbeat, hands the screen to a red GUILT bar that only stays full on consistent perfects, fractures into the reference two-lane fourth-beat gimmick, and returns to a fast one-lane run. The memory rises through static, determination opens six lanes, a whiteout cuts to black four-lane false guilt with a decorative bar that cannot refill, and the dawn returns the ocean, adds flowers, hides the notes, and turns the sync bar into a full rainbow.
- **Guilt engine:** during INTENTION's guilt movements the red bar drains with note density and receives a small refill for every perfect/great/good, so sparse phrases are forgiving and dense phrases demand accuracy. The later fake bar is decorative: it drains slowly toward a crack, never refills, and does not affect scoring.
- **Feedback:** perfect/great/good/bad/miss windows, combo, score, accuracy, sync meter, hit bursts, shockwaves, screen flashes, and rank screen.
- **Results:** animated “COMPILING RESULTS” transition followed by a full results layout with score, accuracy ring, judgement bars, combo trace, rank, and new-best delta.
- **Pause safely:** `Esc` or the pause button freezes both the transport and the chart; switching tabs/windows pauses automatically.
- **Responsive:** landscape and portrait layouts, safe-area padding, multi-touch pointer capture, no page scrolling during play.

### Controls

`A S D F J K L ;`, numpad `1–8`, or tap/click anywhere along a lane. During CHRONOSTASIS's STASIS breakdown, `Space` or a tap on the centre target hits the pendulum. `Esc` pauses.

### Development

```bash
npm install
npm run dev     # http://localhost:3002
npm run build   # static bundle in dist/
```

The playfield is Three.js with an Unreal Bloom pass; audio transport is Web Audio so pause/resume freezes the chart and the music together.

### Chart tooling

```bash
node tools/analyze-audio.mjs input.wav analysis.json
node tools/build-charts.mjs cryout-analysis.json world-analysis.json chronostasis-analysis.json
node tools/build-boss-chart.mjs   # reads tools/source/untouchable-onsets.json
node tools/build-intention-chart.mjs   # reads tools/source/intention-onsets.json
```

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Finish the CRYOUT game, including a complete Intention boss track, while preserving existing tracks and gameplay.
- Improve the Intention boss animation and gameplay responsiveness according to the supplied video references.

## Requirements
- Intention is a 180 BPM boss track with its own chart, visuals, camera choreography, gameplay gimmicks, and GUILT-style meter.
- Follow the requested timeline: ocean/Libra reveal, lane spin and bounce, pillar boss sequence, top-down Libra and glitching “INTENTIONS,” heartbeat and GUILT phases, faster one-lane sections, two-lane glitch pattern, return to ocean, GUILT memory, bright ending, whiteout, and final dawn.
- Reduce holds outside suitable sections and add them where the music supports them.
- Boss camera movement should be free and dramatic rather than constrained to the hit area; hit position should follow the camera.
- Make boss animation substantially more dynamic (“10000 times cooler”); make the spinning one-lane boss fast, with notes present immediately as the lane appears so the player can tap quickly without waiting for notes to arrive.
- Remake the Intention boss intro so it is unlike the previous boss intro and contains no note animation.
- Use the supplied videos as visual references, including `/tmp/opencode/uploads/b33eb5db-1b34-4977-a3e1-bdad98c61cb9/Record_2026-11-19-05-01-00.mp4`.

## Decisions
- Treat the supplied audio as 213.505 seconds long; timestamps are minutes:seconds, including apparent typos such as “0:175” and “1:145.”
- Use offline audio analysis to guide tempo and charting, while checking the audio and reference videos.

## Work State
### Completed
- Existing four-track game, including “The Untouchable of f RA IA’s Land,” is integrated.
- Added `public/audio/intention.mp3`, an Intention chart generator and generated chart, and initial Intention stage/gameplay integration.
- `npm run build` succeeds; previous autoplay checks reported clears for all five tracks.

### Active
- Redesign the Intention boss intro to be distinct from the previous boss and contain no note animation.
- Expand boss camera choreography and make hit position follow the freely moving camera.
- Make the one-lane spinning boss fast and make notes immediately tappable as the lane appears.
- Review chart timing, tempo, holds, and two-lane pattern against audio and references.
- Verify visual phases, GUILT drain/refill behavior, and regressions across existing tracks.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the current Intention boss intro, camera choreography, and one-lane note spawning in the implementation.
2. Implement the distinct no-note intro, freer camera movement with a following hit position, and fast immediately playable one-lane sections.
3. Build and run browser gameplay checks for Intention and all existing tracks; inspect relevant logs and screenshots.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Track selection, gameplay, scoring/results, and track-specific logic.
- `src/scene.js`: Three.js stage, camera, lane visuals, and effects.
- `src/intention-stage.js`: Intention-specific stage visuals and phase transitions.
- `src/charts/intention.js`: Generated Intention chart.
- `tools/build-intention-chart.mjs`: Intention chart generator and event timeline.
- `src/tracks.js`: Track registration and metadata.
- `src/audio.js`: Audio loading and buffer selection.
- `src/style.css`: Menus, HUD, overlays, and meter presentation.
- `index.html`: App structure and HUD elements.
- `/tmp/opencode/uploads/b33eb5db-1b34-4977-a3e1-bdad98c61cb9/Record_2026-11-19-05-01-00.mp4`: New boss-animation reference.
- `/tmp/opencode/uploads/17a05b34-4a76-4724-a602-d72513b2cb62/New Project 10 [D3CED89].mp4`: Earlier visual reference.
- `/tmp/opencode/analysis.json`: Offline audio-analysis output.
- `/tmp/opencode/timeline.txt`: Windowed tempo and energy estimates.
- `/tmp/opencode/verify/autoplay-five.log`: Latest five-track autoplay test output.

## Important Context
- Repository changes are uncommitted; prior modified files include `README.md`, `index.html`, `src/main.js`, `src/scene.js`, `src/style.css`, and `src/audio.js`, plus added Intention files and audio.
- A prior guilt test scheduled autoplay too late, after gameplay began, causing 166 misses; later perfect hits demonstrated GUILT refilling, but that run does not validate early scoring.

34:Charts are generated offline from beat/onset analysis, then committed as static data in `src/charts/`. Each track has its own event recipe: CRYOUT keeps its authored 4/6/8-lane chart and signal accents, WORLD uses city/atmospheric accents, CHRONOSTASIS derives its ticks, bursts, clock windows, and pendulum taps from its analysed motif peaks, and THE UNTOUCHABLE is built from a dedicated onset analysis with an explicit tempo map. INTENTION uses a dedicated onset/tempo analysis and an event score for its ocean, libra, guilt and dawn movements. Track metadata lives in `src/tracks.js`.
35-
36-### Gameplay
37-
38-- **Track selection:** pick any of the five tracks from the start screen. Audio decodes per track and is cached, and personal bests are stored per track in `localStorage`. A run that clears a track (50% accuracy or better) marks its card, and the picker header tracks how many of the five have been cleared.
39-- **Dynamic lane count:** charts move through 4, 6, and 8-lane sections; the field spacing, ring scale, note scale, camera and hit zones re-frame themselves around the playable lanes.
40-- **Tap the whole lane:** invisible tap strips start at the hit circle, run straight up the lane along its projected angle, extend below the ring for thumbs, and widen to fill the gap between neighbouring lanes. Pressing never draws an overlay — all feedback is in the 3D field.
41-- **Incoming lanes unlock early:** a lane with a note on the way becomes tappable before its section officially starts, so notes never arrive on a hidden lane.
42-- **Holds:** keep at least one finger anywhere on the screen to sustain every active hold. Releasing one thumb won't break another lane's hold.
43-- **Moving lanes:** lanes fan, wave, slope, zigzag, and orbit with each section; notes and hold bodies are parented to the lane frame so they follow the same diagonal.
44-- **Unused-lane echoes:** dormant lanes emit directional beat echoes that drift sideways, slow down, and fade.
--
48-- **Cathedral overture:** THE UNTOUCHABLE opens with 28.5 lane-less seconds inside a procedural gothic nave. The camera cuts down the aisle on the beat, stained glass and title cards carry the story, and the playfield stays hidden until the clock chamber arrives.
49-- **Wind instead of idle lanes:** in THE UNTOUCHABLE's boss stage any lane that is not playable becomes a stream of 3D wind ribbons that sweep through X, Y and Z while spinning, so the unused field is part of the scene instead of empty tracks.
50-- **Free-flight clock stage:** after the overture the nave becomes the playfield and notes travel on curved X/Z paths before converging on their lane rings at the hit line. The boss chart follows a 111.1 → 96 → 111.1 BPM map, and every camera, glitch, caption and clock tick event is keyed to the analysed song. A framing guard measures the live rings and the clock crown after each authored camera move, then only adjusts pitch, lens or distance when the hit line or the crown would leave the frame, so the cinematic direction survives on desktop and phone aspect ratios.
51:- **INTENTION's four memories:** a black-particle overture with white lanes opens onto an ocean under dark clouds, a golden libra, four cardinal pillars, and a spinning halo star. A one-lane corkscrew snaps back to the field, the camera leans toward the lane that just answered, and the top-down libra shot carries a glitching INTENTIONS title. The chart then distorts into a heartbeat, hands the screen to a red GUILT bar that only stays full on consistent perfects, fractures into the reference two-lane fourth-beat gimmick, and returns to a fast one-lane run. The memory rises through static, determination opens six lanes, a whiteout cuts to black four-lane false guilt with a decorative bar that cannot refill, and the dawn returns the ocean, adds flowers, hides the notes, and turns the sync bar into a full rainbow.
52:- **Guilt engine:** during INTENTION's guilt movements the red bar drains with note density and receives a small refill for every perfect/great/good, so sparse phrases are forgiving and dense phrases demand accuracy. The later fake bar is decorative: it drains slowly toward a crack, never refills, and does not affect scoring.
53-- **Feedback:** perfect/great/good/bad/miss windows, combo, score, accuracy, sync meter, hit bursts, shockwaves, screen flashes, and rank screen.
54-- **Results:** animated “COMPILING RESULTS” transition followed by a full results layout with score, accuracy ring, judgement bars, combo trace, rank, and new-best delta.
55-- **Pause safely:** `Esc` or the pause button freezes both the transport and the chart; switching tabs/windows pauses automatically.
56-- **Responsive:** landscape and portrait layouts, safe-area padding, multi-touch pointer capture, no page scrolling during play.

 - **Frozen pendulum:** during the STASIS breakdown the clock stops and one lane becomes an antique pendulum. It swings left and right over a centre target while music-note glyphs float around it; tap the centre (click/tap the target or press `Space`) each time the bob crosses the middle. The gimmick runs until the next clock event and then hands the screen back to the lane chart.
 - **Cathedral overture:** THE UNTOUCHABLE opens with 28.5 lane-less seconds inside a procedural gothic nave. The camera cuts down the aisle on the beat, stained glass and title cards carry the story, and the playfield stays hidden until the clock chamber arrives.
 - **Wind instead of idle lanes:** in THE UNTOUCHABLE's boss stage any lane that is not playable becomes a stream of 3D wind ribbons that sweep through X, Y and Z while spinning, so the unused field is part of the scene instead of empty tracks.
 - **Free-flight clock stage:** after the overture the nave becomes the playfield and notes travel on curved X/Z paths before converging on their lane rings at the hit line. The boss chart follows a 111.1 → 96 → 111.1 BPM map, and every camera, glitch, caption and clock tick event is keyed to the analysed song. A framing guard measures the live rings and the clock crown after each authored camera move, then only adjusts pitch, lens or distance when the hit line or the crown would leave the frame, so the cinematic direction survives on desktop and phone aspect ratios.

## CRYOUT — Dynamic 3D Rhythm

A browser rhythm game built around a flat, bold hit-circle language placed inside a moving 3D field. Five fully charted tracks are included, each with its own section map, lane motion, effects, and difficulty curve.

### Tracks

| Track | BPM | Difficulty | Lanes | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **CRYOUT** | 100 | Advanced | 4 · 6 · 8 | 328 notes · 6 holds |
| **WORLD YEARNING FOR AN END** | 120 | Hard | 4 · 6 | 448 notes · 5 holds |
| **CHRONOSTASIS** | 99.4 | Expert | 4 · 6 | 432 notes · 1 hold · 8 pendulum taps |
| **THE UNTOUCHABLE OF f RA IA'S LAND** | 111.1 / 96 | Boss | 4 · 6 · 8 | 407 notes · 4 holds · 243 events |
| **INTENTION** | 180 / 195 | Boss | 1 · 2 · 4 · 6 | 596 notes · 26 holds · 239 events |

Charts are generated offline from beat/onset analysis, then committed as static data in `src/charts/`. Each track has its own event recipe: CRYOUT keeps its authored 4/6/8-lane chart and signal accents, WORLD uses city/atmospheric accents, CHRONOSTASIS derives its ticks, bursts, clock windows, and pendulum taps from its analysed motif peaks, and THE UNTOUCHABLE is built from a dedicated onset analysis with an explicit tempo map. INTENTION uses a dedicated onset/tempo analysis and an event score for its ocean, libra, guilt and dawn movements. Track metadata lives in `src/tracks.js`.

### Gameplay

- **Track selection:** pick any of the five tracks from the start screen. Audio decodes per track and is cached, and personal bests are stored per track in `localStorage`. A run that clears a track (50% accuracy or better) marks its card, and the picker header tracks how many of the five have been cleared.
- **Dynamic lane count:** charts move through 4, 6, and 8-lane sections; the field spacing, ring scale, note scale, camera and hit zones re-frame themselves around the playable lanes.
- **Tap the whole lane:** invisible tap strips start at the hit circle, run straight up the lane along its projected angle, extend below the ring for thumbs, and widen to fill the gap between neighbouring lanes. Pressing never draws an overlay — all feedback is in the 3D field.
- **Incoming lanes unlock early:** a lane with a note on the way becomes tappable before its section officially starts, so notes never arrive on a hidden lane.
- **Holds:** keep at least one finger anywhere on the screen to sustain every active hold. Releasing one thumb won't break another lane's hold.
- **Moving lanes:** lanes fan, wave, slope, zigzag, and orbit with each section; notes and hold bodies are parented to the lane frame so they follow the same diagonal.
- **Unused-lane echoes:** dormant lanes emit directional beat echoes that drift sideways, slow down, and fade.
- **City intro:** the second track layers a two-plane parallax skyline behind the field during its intro, break, and outro.
- **Clockwork background:** CHRONOSTASIS turns the two unused outer lanes into a background clock. The slow hand sweeps while the fast hand ticks on the beat; the chart starts the clock at motif boundaries, freezes it during the breakdown, and speeds it up for the final section.
- **Frozen pendulum:** during the STASIS breakdown the clock stops and one lane becomes an antique pendulum. It swings left and right over a centre target while music-note glyphs float around it; tap the centre (click/tap the target or press `Space`) each time the bob crosses the middle. The gimmick runs until the next clock event and then hands the screen back to the lane chart.
- **Cathedral overture:** THE UNTOUCHABLE opens with 28.5 lane-less seconds inside a procedural gothic nave. The camera cuts down the aisle on the beat, stained glass and title cards carry the story, and the playfield stays hidden until the clock chamber arrives.
- **Wind instead of idle lanes:** in THE UNTOUCHABLE's boss stage any lane that is not playable becomes a stream of 3D wind ribbons that sweep through X, Y and Z while spinning, so the unused field is part of the scene instead of empty tracks.
- **Free-flight clock stage:** after the overture the nave becomes the playfield and notes travel on curved X/Z paths before converging on their lane rings at the hit line. The boss chart follows a 111.1 → 96 → 111.1 BPM map, and every camera, glitch, caption and clock tick event is keyed to the analysed song. A framing guard measures the live rings and the clock crown after each authored camera move, then only adjusts pitch, lens or distance when the hit line or the crown would leave the frame, so the cinematic direction survives on desktop and phone aspect ratios.
- **INTENTION's four memories:** a black-particle overture with white lanes opens onto an ocean under dark clouds, a golden libra, four cardinal pillars, and a spinning halo star. A one-lane corkscrew snaps back to the field, the camera leans toward the lane that just answered, and the top-down libra shot carries a glitching INTENTIONS title. The chart then distorts into a heartbeat, hands the screen to a red GUILT bar that only stays full on consistent perfects, fractures into the reference two-lane fourth-beat gimmick, and returns to a fast one-lane run. The memory rises through static, determination opens six lanes, a whiteout cuts to black four-lane false guilt with a decorative bar that cannot refill, and the dawn returns the ocean, adds flowers, hides the notes, and turns the sync bar into a full rainbow. Gameplay is intentionally textless: score, judgement, lane labels, HUD copy and mid-song captions are hidden, leaving only the floating rings, meters and cutscene title cards.
- **Guilt engine:** during INTENTION's guilt movements the red bar drains with note density and receives a small refill for every perfect/great/good, so sparse phrases are forgiving and dense phrases demand accuracy. The later fake bar is decorative: it drains slowly toward a crack, never refills, and does not affect scoring.
- **Feedback:** perfect/great/good/bad/miss windows, combo, score, accuracy, sync meter, hit bursts, shockwaves, screen flashes, and rank screen.
- **Results:** animated “COMPILING RESULTS” transition followed by a full results layout with score, accuracy ring, judgement bars, combo trace, rank, and new-best delta.
- **Pause safely:** `Esc` or the pause button freezes both the transport and the chart; switching tabs/windows pauses automatically.
- **Responsive:** landscape and portrait layouts, safe-area padding, multi-touch pointer capture, no page scrolling during play.

### Controls

`A S D F J K L ;`, numpad `1–8`, or tap/click anywhere along a lane. During CHRONOSTASIS's STASIS breakdown, `Space` or a tap on the centre target hits the pendulum. `Esc` pauses.

Charts are generated offline from beat/onset analysis, then committed as static data in `src/charts/`. One shared generator, `tools/build-game-charts.mjs`, rebuilds all five charts from the authored section maps and the decoded onset files in `tools/source/`. Every section is charted as a four-bar phrase (A A' B C): rhythmic cells come from a groove library keyed to the section's energy, weak slots are thinned against the real onsets, lanes follow bounded figures with hand-safe repeats, chords are reserved for phrase peaks, and long same-lane gaps become holds. Accent events are regenerated from bar energy, while boss camera/glitch cues, CHRONOSTASIS's clock/pendulum score, and INTENTION's memory/guilt cues are copied verbatim from `tools/source/gimmick-events.json`, so every gimmick stays choreographed to the record. Track metadata lives in `src/tracks.js`.

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run charts` | Rebuild all five charts from the committed analyses and section maps. |
| `node tools/analyze-mp3.mjs` | Optional: decode the MP3s in Chromium and refresh the CRYOUT / WORLD / CHRONOSTASIS onset analyses. |

The older `tools/build-charts.mjs`, `tools/build-boss-chart.mjs`, and `tools/build-intention-chart.mjs` scripts are kept as the historical per-track builders; the shared generator is the canonical pipeline now.
input.oldString: Charts are generated offline from beat/onset analysis, then committed as static data in `src/charts/`. Each track has its own event recipe: CRYOUT keeps its authored 4/6/8-lane chart and signal accents, WORLD uses city/atmospheric accents, CHRONOSTASIS derives its ticks, bursts, clock windows, and pendulum taps from its analysed motif peaks, and THE UNTOUCHABLE is built from a dedicated onset analysis with an explicit tempo map. INTENTION uses a dedicated onset/tempo analysis and an event score for its ocean, libra, guilt and dawn movements. Track metadata lives in `src/tracks.js`.

 ### Gameplay
 
 - **Track selection:** pick any of the five tracks from the start screen. Audio decodes per track and is cached, and personal bests are stored per track in `localStorage`. A run that clears a track (50% accuracy or better) marks its card, and the picker header tracks how many of the five have been cleared.
 - **Dynamic lane count:** charts move through 4, 6, and 8-lane sections; the field spacing, ring scale, note scale, camera and hit zones re-frame themselves around the playable lanes.

## Objective
- Remake all five game charts and consolidate chart generation into a reproducible shared pipeline while preserving track-specific gimmicks and Intention’s textless gameplay presentation.

## Requirements
- Regenerate and validate charts for CRYOUT, WORLD YEARNING FOR AN END, CHRONOSTASIS, THE UNTOUCHABLE OF f RA IA'S LAND, and INTENTION.
- Preserve existing timing, holds, lane mechanics, cutscenes, boss phases, and track-specific effects.
- Keep Intention gameplay text hidden; retain title cards for overture/dawn cutscenes and its visual meters/effects.
- Finish with a passing build and browser validation across every track.

## Decisions
- Use one canonical phrase-based chart generator for all tracks.
- Chart notes in four-bar `A A' B C` phrases from energy-selected groove cells, onset snapping, bounded lane figures, phrase-peak chords, and same-lane holds.
- Preserve authored section maps and gimmick event scores rather than regenerating them procedurally.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `tools/build-game-charts.mjs` and `npm run charts`.
- Added decoded MP3 onset-analysis inputs and a reproducible Chromium-based analyser.
- Rebuilt charts:
  - CRYOUT: 390 notes, 12 holds.
  - WORLD: 444 notes, 10 holds.
  - CHRONOSTASIS: 436 notes, 10 holds.
  - UNTOUCHABLE: 374 notes, 8 holds.
  - INTENTION: 532 notes, 19 holds.
- Preserved CHRONOSTASIS clock/pendulum/swings and UNTOUCHABLE boss camera/glitch/caption/wind/tick events.
- Preserved INTENTION GUILT phases, fake guilt, heartbeat, dawn, camera, glitch, and cutscene events.
- Built the production bundle successfully.
- Accelerated browser autoplay cleared all five tracks with full combos, no missed notes, no health loss, and no console/page errors.
- Captured gameplay screenshots and verified staged visuals for CHRONOSTASIS, UNTOUCHABLE, WORLD, and INTENTION.
- Verified section maps and gimmick events match the source maps exactly.
- Confirmed chart generation is deterministic.
- Updated README chart documentation and the gameplay pipeline description.

### Active
- (none)

### Blocked
- (none)

### Completed
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Commit the uncommitted chart, generator, analysis, documentation, package, and production-dist changes if repository publishing is required.

## Relevant Files
- `tools/build-game-charts.mjs`: Canonical all-track chart generator.
- `tools/analyze-mp3.mjs`: Browser-based MP3 onset/tempo analyser.
- `tools/source/gimmick-events.json`: Preserved boss, clock, pendulum, and INTENTION gimmick events.
- `tools/source/section-maps.json`: Authored visual and lane section maps.
- `src/charts/`: Regenerated chart data for all five tracks.
- `src/intention-stage.js`: INTENTION boss implementation and visual effects.
- `src/main.js`: Chart playback, judging, hold handling, and autoplay/debug integration.
- `src/style.css`: INTENTION textless HUD and presentation.
- `src/tracks.js`: Track metadata and chart registration.
- `README.md`: Updated charting pipeline and track information.
- `package.json`: Added `npm run charts`.
- `dist/`: Rebuilt production output.

## Important Context
- Repository changes remain uncommitted.
- Full-chart autoplay used accelerated playback and previously reported all 444/436/374/532/390-note runs as perfect clears where applicable.
- Intention ended in the dawn phase with `notesHidden: true`; text remains hidden outside cutscenes.
- The old per-track builders remain historical scripts; `tools/build-game-charts.mjs` is now canonical.

A browser rhythm game built around a flat, bold hit-circle language placed inside a moving 3D field. Five fully charted tracks are included, each with its own section map, lane motion, effects, and difficulty curve.

### Tracks

| Track | BPM | Difficulty | Lanes | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **CRYOUT** | 100 | Advanced | 4 · 6 · 8 | 390 notes · 12 holds |
| **WORLD YEARNING FOR AN END** | 120 | Hard | 4 · 6 | 444 notes · 10 holds |
| **CHRONOSTASIS** | 99.4 | Expert | 4 · 6 | 436 notes · 10 holds · 8 pendulum taps |
| **THE UNTOUCHABLE OF f RA IA'S LAND** | 111.1 / 96 | Boss | 4 · 6 · 8 | 374 notes · 8 holds · 229 events |
| **INTENTION** | 180 / 195 | Boss | 1 · 2 · 4 · 6 | 532 notes · 19 holds · 284 events |

Charts are generated offline from beat/onset analysis, then committed as static data in `src/charts/`. One shared generator, `tools/build-game-charts.mjs`, rebuilds all five charts from the authored section maps and the decoded onset files in `tools/source/`. Every section is charted as a four-bar phrase (A A' B C): rhythmic cells come from a groove library keyed to the section's energy, weak slots are thinned against the real onsets, lanes follow bounded figures with hand-safe repeats, chords are reserved for phrase peaks, and long same-lane gaps become holds. Accent events are regenerated from bar energy, while boss camera/glitch cues, CHRONOSTASIS's clock/pendulum score, and INTENTION's memory/guilt cues are copied verbatim from `tools/source/gimmick-events.json`, so every gimmick stays choreographed to the record. Track metadata lives in `src/tracks.js`.

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run charts` | Rebuild all five charts from the committed analyses and section maps. |
| `node tools/analyze-mp3.mjs` | Optional: decode the MP3s in Chromium and refresh the CRYOUT / WORLD / CHRONOSTASIS onset analyses. |

The older `tools/build-charts.mjs`, `tools/build-boss-chart.mjs`, and `tools/build-intention-chart.mjs` scripts are kept as the historical per-track builders; the shared generator is the canonical pipeline now.

### Gameplay

- **Track selection:** pick any of the five tracks from the start screen. Audio decodes per track and is cached, and personal bests are stored per track in `localStorage`. A run that clears a track (50% accuracy or better) marks its card, and the picker header tracks how many of the five have been cleared.
- **Dynamic lane count:** charts move through 4, 6, and 8-lane sections; the field spacing, ring scale, note scale, camera and hit zones re-frame themselves around the playable lanes.
- **Tap the whole lane:** invisible tap strips start at the hit circle, run straight up the lane along its projected angle, extend below the ring for thumbs, and widen to fill the gap between neighbouring lanes. Pressing never draws an overlay — all feedback is in the 3D field.
- **Incoming lanes unlock early:** a lane with a note on the way becomes tappable before its section officially starts, so notes never arrive on a hidden lane.
- **Holds:** keep at least one finger anywhere on the screen to sustain every active hold. Releasing one thumb won't break another lane's hold.
- **Moving lanes:** lanes fan, wave, slope, zigzag, and orbit with each section; notes and hold bodies are parented to the lane frame so they follow the same diagonal.
- **Unused-lane echoes:** dormant lanes emit directional beat echoes that drift sideways, slow down, and fade.
- **City intro:** the second track layers a two-plane parallax skyline behind the field during its intro, break, and outro.
- **Clockwork background:** CHRONOSTASIS turns the two unused outer lanes into a background clock. The slow hand sweeps while the fast hand ticks on the beat; the chart starts the clock at motif boundaries, freezes it during the breakdown, and speeds it up for the final section.
- **Frozen pendulum:** during the STASIS breakdown the clock stops and one lane becomes an antique pendulum. It swings left and right over a centre target while music-note glyphs float around it; tap the centre (click/tap the target or press `Space`) each time the bob crosses the middle. The gimmick runs until the next clock event and then hands the screen back to the lane chart.
- **Cathedral overture:** THE UNTOUCHABLE opens with 28.5 lane-less seconds inside a procedural gothic nave. The camera cuts down the aisle on the beat, stained glass and title cards carry the story, and the playfield stays hidden until the clock chamber arrives.
- **Wind instead of idle lanes:** in THE UNTOUCHABLE's boss stage any lane that is not playable becomes a stream of 3D wind ribbons that sweep through X, Y and Z while spinning, so the unused field is part of the scene instead of empty tracks.
- **Free-flight clock stage:** after the overture the nave becomes the playfield and notes travel on curved X/Z paths before converging on their lane rings at the hit line. The boss chart follows a 111.1 → 96 → 111.1 BPM map, and every camera, glitch, caption and clock tick event is keyed to the analysed song. A framing guard measures the live rings and the clock crown after each authored camera move, then only adjusts pitch, lens or distance when the hit line or the crown would leave the frame, so the cinematic direction survives on desktop and phone aspect ratios.
- **INTENTION's four memories:** a black-particle overture with white lanes opens onto an ocean under dark clouds, a golden libra, four cardinal pillars, and a spinning halo star. A one-lane corkscrew snaps back to the field, the camera leans toward the lane that just answered, and the top-down libra shot carries a glitching INTENTIONS title. The chart then distorts into a heartbeat, hands the screen to a red GUILT bar that only stays full on consistent perfects, fractures into the reference two-lane fourth-beat gimmick, and returns to a fast one-lane run. The memory rises through static, determination opens six lanes, a whiteout cuts to black four-lane false guilt with a decorative bar that cannot refill, and the dawn returns the ocean, adds flowers, hides the notes, and turns the sync bar into a full rainbow. Gameplay is intentionally textless: score, judgement, lane labels, HUD copy and mid-song captions are hidden, leaving only the floating rings, meters and cutscene title cards.
- **Guilt engine:** during INTENTION's guilt movements the red bar drains with note density and receives a small refill for every perfect/great/good, so sparse phrases are forgiving and dense phrases demand accuracy. The later fake bar is decorative: it drains slowly toward a crack, never refills, and does not affect scoring.
- **Feedback:** perfect/great/good/bad/miss windows, combo, score, accuracy, sync meter, hit bursts, shockwaves, screen flashes, and rank screen.
- **Results:** animated “COMPILING RESULTS” transition followed by a full results layout with score, accuracy ring, judgement bars, combo trace, rank, and new-best delta.
- **Pause safely:** `Esc` or the pause button freezes both the transport and the chart; switching tabs/windows pauses automatically.
- **Responsive:** landscape and portrait layouts, safe-area padding, multi-touch pointer capture, no page scrolling during play.

### Controls

`A S D F J K L ;`, numpad `1–8`, or tap/click anywhere along a lane. During CHRONOSTASIS's STASIS breakdown, `Space` or a tap on the centre target hits the pendulum. `Esc` pauses.

### Development

```bash
npm install
npm run dev     # http://localhost:3002
npm run build   # static bundle in dist/
```

The playfield is Three.js with an Unreal Bloom pass; audio transport is Web Audio so pause/resume freezes the chart and the music together.

### Chart tooling

```bash
node tools/analyze-audio.mjs input.wav analysis.json
node tools/build-charts.mjs cryout-analysis.json world-analysis.json chronostasis-analysis.json
node tools/build-boss-chart.mjs   # reads tools/source/untouchable-onsets.json
node tools/build-intention-chart.mjs   # reads tools/source/intention-onsets.json
```

The original Cryout chart is preserved in `tools/source/cryout-legacy.json`. The analyser reads mono 16-bit WAV; the repository MP3s can be decoded to that format offline before analysis. The chart builder derives clock windows and accents from detected motif peaks, so adding another song does not reuse the same event layout. The boss chart builder maps the overture, clock chamber and finale onto the analysed onset grid and writes the full event score used by the cathedral stage.

## Objective
- Finish and deliver the five-track rhythm game with a reproducible chart pipeline and validated gameplay presentation.

## Requirements
- Remake and validate charts for CRYOUT, WORLD YEARNING FOR AN END, CHRONOSTASIS, THE UNTOUCHABLE OF f RA IA'S LAND, and INTENTION.
- Preserve each track’s timing, holds, lane mechanics, gimmick events, boss phases, cutscenes, and track-specific visuals.
- Keep INTENTION gameplay text hidden while retaining overture/dawn title cards and its visual meters/effects.
- Finish with passing builds and browser validation across every track.

## Decisions
- Use `tools/build-game-charts.mjs` as the canonical chart generator with four-bar `A A' B C` phrases.
- Keep authored section maps and gimmick event scores intact rather than regenerating them procedurally.
- Use global tap/click/key input that claims the closest pending note rather than lane-tied tap areas.
- Run the game-over sequence on wall-clock time for consistent 3.7-second behavior.

- Regenerated all five charts and consolidated chart generation under `npm run charts`.
- Preserved CHRONOSTASIS clock, pendulum, and swing events.

- Restored the tape-stop, camera pull-back, `SIGNAL LOST` flatline, and results flow for the fail state.

- `tools/build-game-chards.mjs`: Canonical chart generator.

- `tools/source/gimmick-events.json`: Preserved boss and track gimmick events.
